methodological_rigor.justification: Sophisticated preclinical design employing conditional knockout mice (Sting1-cKO, Tox-cKO) with multiple complementary methodologies: in vitro co-culture, single-cell and bulk RNA-seq, flow cytometry, immunofluorescence, and in vivo adoptive cell therapy models across three tumor types (TC-1, MC38, B16F10). RNA-seq data publicly deposited (GSA-CRA011572). However, mouse cohorts are relatively small (4-5 per group), and no prospective power calculation is provided.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Preclinical mechanistic study identifying STING-TOX-HO-1 regulatory axis governing CD8+ T cell ferroptosis in tumor microenvironment. Findings suggest therapeutic strategies (STING inhibition, TOX deletion, MCT1 inhibition) with synergy demonstrated in mouse models. However, clinical translation is speculative; no human validation or clinical trial data provided. Relevance depends on translational validation.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods comprehensively describe mouse generation, cell culture, tumor models, molecular assays (qPCR, RNA-seq, flow cytometry, immunofluorescence), and statistical analyses. RNA-seq and scRNA-seq data deposited in public repositories (GSA-CRA011572, GSA-Human: HRA003358, GEO: GSE162025). Missing elements: explicit sample size justification, blinding/randomization details beyond gender notation, formal statistical analysis plan prior to experiments.

novelty_literature.justification: Identifies STING-TOX-HO-1 as a regulatory axis driving CD8+ T cell ferroptosis, revealing unexpected synergy between two known regulators. Lactate as upstream trigger of this pathway is novel. Links iron accumulation, mitochondrial oxidative stress, and ferroptosis in immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Substantially extends prior work on TOX-mediated T cell exhaustion and STING signaling by identifying ferroptosis as mechanism.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized manuscript with clear section structure. Methods systematically describe mouse models, assays, and analytical approaches. Figures effectively integrate multiple data layers (Figure 2: genomic landscape with clinical/phenotypic integration). Figure legends appropriately detailed. Some technical density in Methods section reflects preclinical complexity; overall communication is clear.

key_strengths: Rigorous mechanistic approach employing conditional knockout mice with multiple complementary assays (RNA-seq, flow, immunofluorescence, biochemistry)
Novel identification of STING-TOX-HO-1 axis as regulator of CD8+ ferroptosis with lactate as upstream environmental trigger
Demonstration of synergy with immunotherapy (ICB, chemotherapy, STING agonist) in multiple murine tumor models
Public data deposition of RNA-seq datasets enabling independent verification and secondary analysis
Integration of mechanistic and transcriptomic evidence supporting ferroptotic pathway in CD8+ T cells
key_concerns: Preclinical stage limits clinical applicability; mouse model ferroptosis may not recapitulate human immune dysfunction
Small sample sizes for mouse cohorts (4-5 per group) without power calculation or formal sample size justification
No multiple testing correction explicitly stated despite numerous hypothesis tests across omics and flow datasets
Limited human validation: only 123 historical patient samples for IHC without prospective cohort or clinical correlation
Mechanism of ferroptosis vs. other CD8+ death pathways not formally distinguished in functional assays
chief_reviewer.rationale: Methodologically sophisticated preclinical study with novel mechanistic insights linking known regulators through unexpected ferroptosis pathway. Tier 2 placement reflects novelty and rigor, though clinical translation requires validation.
